candidates.alive_premise: One partner tries to throw away the evidence of everything that did not work. The other reveals they kept it because those failures show how the person they love was made.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis about a partner preserving rejected applications, abandoned drafts, or failed-attempt artifacts; no Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed.
candidates.title: The Box of Almosts
candidates.concrete_moment: During a cupboard clear-out, one partner finds a battered box containing an early rejection, crossed-out draft, expired pass, and other failed versions. The owner reaches to discard them; the keeper lays them in chronological order beside the current work that finally exists.
candidates.universal_truth: Being witnessed in love is not only having someone celebrate who you became; it is having someone remember the unsuccessful versions that carried you there.
candidates.audience_mirror: People whose partner saw the rejected applications, abandoned projects, awkward beginnings, or repeated restarts behind the version everyone else now praises.
candidates.scroll_stop: A person empties an apparent box of rubbish while their partner catches one crumpled page before it reaches the bin.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: Keeping someone’s failures can look backward-facing, yet the archive proves that their struggle was seen and their becoming was never invisible.
scene_proof: Worn papers, badges, and drafts fall toward a discard pile during a cupboard clear-out.
The partner catches one crumpled artifact before it reaches the bin.
The artifacts are arranged by date, each visibly different and increasingly developed.
The latest completed work is placed beside the oldest failed version while both partners remain physically present with the evidence.
candidates.relationship_motion: One partner moves from erasing the embarrassing past to examining it; the other moves from silent keeper to active witness, then returns the choice of what to keep.
retention_ladder: Why is the partner rescuing rubbish from the bin?
The first artifact reveals a rejection, but not why it matters.
More dated attempts establish that the keeping was deliberate.
The chronological arrangement reveals visible growth.
The current work completes the turn: the box held the making, not the loss.
candidates.payoff: The achievement may belong to one person, but the history of becoming belongs partly to the person who stayed close enough to remember every almost.
candidates.dm_send_reason: A viewer can send it to the partner who remembers their rejected or unfinished versions with the meaning: you saw the part nobody applauded.
candidates.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel built as a cupboard-clear-out scene with a delayed chronological reveal.
candidates.asot_turn: Make the romance live in the slightly absurd domestic fact that one person’s throwaway pile is the other person’s fiercely kept evidence, without turning either partner into a rescuer.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: cupboard purge + saved failure artifacts + chronological arrangement + apparent cruelty reverses into witnessed becoming
risks: Could become a static paper-artifact carousel unless every beat shows handling, resistance, and changed body language.
The final motion must return ownership and consent to the person whose work it is.
A real artifact trail requires creator confirmation before Aachu/Zuv personalization.

candidates.alive_premise: Before every intimidating new beginning, one partner records the same few seconds at the doorway. Years later, the repeated frame reveals courage growing before either person noticed.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis about a couple recording the same doorway moment before successive first days; no Aachu/Zuv ritual or footage archive is claimed.
candidates.title: Every First Day, Same Doorway
candidates.concrete_moment: Before several first days, one partner pauses at a doorway while the other records the same short gesture: turn back, nervous face, reluctant wave, enter. On the newest first day, the sequence reveals hesitation becoming ownership.
candidates.universal_truth: A long relationship lets someone witness courage before it feels like confidence; change becomes visible when the old thresholds sit beside the new one.
candidates.audience_mirror: Couples who have stood outside each other’s interviews, courses, offices, studios, clinics, or other intimidating beginnings.
candidates.scroll_stop: Four near-identical doorway frames appear together, but the person’s posture changes while the person recording remains the stable witness.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: The ritual looks like repetitive teasing at nervous first-day behavior, but becomes a time record of bravery accumulating.
scene_proof: An early threshold shows tense shoulders, checked papers, and a backward glance.
Later thresholds change setting and wardrobe while preserving the turn-back gesture.
A reverse angle proves the same partner has been recording each beginning.
At the newest threshold, the person crosses confidently and pulls the witness into the final frame.
candidates.relationship_motion: The recorded partner moves from needing a last backward look to crossing with ownership; the recorder moves from observer outside the frame to acknowledged participant.
retention_ladder: Why are the doorway moments repeating?
Dates and changing locations establish time passing.
Posture changes invite comparison.
The recorder is revealed as the stable witness.
The newest repetition breaks when the witness enters the frame.
candidates.payoff: Sometimes the person who filmed your nervous beginnings is the only one who can show you that you stopped asking the doorway for permission.
candidates.dm_send_reason: It thanks the person who stood outside intimidating beginnings and noticed courage before the person crossing did.
candidates.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel with visibly changing thresholds and one stable recording gesture; Reel only if genuine repeated footage exists.
candidates.asot_turn: Treat each threshold as an affectionate character scene, then let the final inclusion of the witness turn a familiar recording habit into relationship proof.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: same threshold across first days + posture evolution + recorder as stable witness + witness enters final frame
risks: Without genuine footage or a creator-confirmed ritual, the route could feel manufactured.
It must avoid the rejected one-more-photo aesthetic by making entry and changed posture the proof.
Each threshold needs a materially different life chapter.

candidates.alive_premise: Everyone else knows the finished version. One partner knows the terrible first version so well they can still perform it from memory.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis about one partner repeatedly witnessing the other rehearse an evolving speech, pitch, routine, story, or creative work; no Aachu/Zuv rehearsal history is claimed.
candidates.title: They Knew the Bad Version by Heart
candidates.concrete_moment: During a polished presentation, one partner in the audience mouths an awkward beat that was removed many drafts ago. Past rehearsals reveal why: the witness heard every false start until the deleted version became shared memory.
candidates.universal_truth: The deepest witness is often not the person who applauds the polished result, but the person who knows the rough version by heart because they were present while it changed.
candidates.audience_mirror: Couples where one person has endured repeated practice runs, unfinished stories, awkward presentations, exam answers, jokes, speeches, or other work-in-progress versions.
candidates.scroll_stop: At the polished presentation, the audience partner performs an obviously wrong old beat at exactly the same time as the person on stage.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: Knowing the obsolete bad version seems like ammunition for teasing, but reveals an intimacy unavailable to the audience applauding the finished work.
scene_proof: The witness anticipates a removed line or gesture during the current polished version.
An earlier rehearsal shows a false start and the witness resetting a timer or taking the familiar practice position.
Successive rehearsals change location, pages, and delivery while the obsolete fragment recurs.
After the public moment, the couple privately reenacts the discarded version together.
candidates.relationship_motion: The maker moves from cringing at the obsolete version to joining the reenactment; the witness moves from rehearsal audience to keeper of a private history.
retention_ladder: Why does the audience partner know a line absent from the finished version?
The first rehearsal reveals it began as a mistake.
Repeated attempts show the witness absorbing the work through proximity.
The polished version removes every trace of the awkward beginning.
The couple deliberately reenacts the bad version together after the applause.
candidates.payoff: Public love can applaud the final version; private love sometimes knows the deleted version by heart.
candidates.dm_send_reason: It is naturally sendable to the partner who heard every practice run and remembers the embarrassing version nobody else knows existed.
candidates.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel with a wrong-beat cold open, rehearsal escalation, polished public contrast, and private reenactment.
candidates.asot_turn: Use affectionate embarrassment and mutual reenactment instead of solemn encouragement; comic muscle memory becomes proof of years spent close to the making.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: obsolete rehearsal beat resurfaces at polished event + witness knows deleted version + comic error becomes intimate history
risks: A generic supportive-partner montage would weaken the route.
The incident needs a creator-confirmed form of repeated practice before personalization.
The witness must not be framed as tolerating a burdensome partner.

candidates.alive_premise: Their two family patterns look incompatible until the hidden halves meet.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis; no Aachu/Zuv canon is claimed. Two authentic family practices would require creator confirmation before personalization.
candidates.title: The Pattern Was Never Supposed to Match
candidates.concrete_moment: At a family gathering, the couple and relatives create two halves of a festive floor pattern behind a divider. When it lifts, the styles differ, but both partners left open edges that connect at the center; both families complete the perimeter together.
candidates.universal_truth: Alignment is not becoming identical; it is leaving an honest place where two different histories can meet.
candidates.audience_mirror: Couples carrying different family customs, regional aesthetics, or inherited ways of celebrating who do not want either side flattened into the other.
candidates.scroll_stop: Two families work on opposite sides of a covered center line while visible voting markers invite a prediction: match, clash, or something else.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: The mismatch appears to prove they built separate worlds, but the unfinished edges reveal that each was designing toward the other.
scene_proof: Different hands, tools, colors, and family methods build two separate halves.
Relatives place guesses before the divider is removed.
The revealed halves do not mirror each other, yet their open paths align at the center.
The couple makes the first joining marks and the families fill the perimeter.
candidates.relationship_motion: Each partner preserves a family language while actively designing a point of welcome for the other; the wider family follows their lead.
retention_ladder: Introduce the hidden halves and family prediction.
Show that the methods and visual languages differ.
Build the expectation of a perfect match or awkward clash.
Reveal intentional open edges rather than sameness.
Let the couple connect the center and the families expand the pattern.
candidates.payoff: What looked like incompatibility becomes proof that neither person had to erase home for the relationship to make a new one.
candidates.dm_send_reason: Someone can send it to a partner from another family culture and mean: I do not need us to match; I want us to make room for both.
candidates.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel built around the divider lift and the before-and-after floor transformation.
candidates.asot_turn: Treat cultural detail as active relationship behavior: hands making space, families reacting, and a shared pattern whose beauty comes from visible difference.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: split family floor art + prediction + different halves with open center + plural belonging end state
risks: Specific practices must be creator-confirmed and culturally accurate.
The pattern cannot function as decoration alone.
The final design must preserve visible difference rather than imply absorption.
